newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand approves 1997 maize import quota.
newsitem.headline: Thailand approves 1997 maize import quota.

text.p: Thailand on Monday approved the commerce ministry's proposal to allow a zero-tariff corn import quota of 200,000 tonnes in 1997, the government spokesman said.
The feed industry must bring in the corn before July when local supplies will become available, said Amnaj Chanawong.

He said the current stock, surveyed March 18-19, was 1.32 million tonnes. The shortfall calculated from demand until June 30, including 30-day stock that must be maintained by the industry, was projected at 345,000 tonnes.
"But we allow 200,000 tonnes as we believe that the gap will be filled by the local supplies which will be available from July," he told reporters.
The agriculture ministry put 1997/98 (July-June) corn output at 4.35 million tonnes from 4.39 million tonnes estimated for 1996/97 season.
Feed industry sources estimated earlier that Thailand would need to import 300,000-400,000 tonnes corn this year.
